task: Repair a public Channel keepalive control after stream ownership moved behind a protocol

subtasks.description: Freeze the dependency-free transfer fixture and its Tornado-derived public contract
lessons: A transfer fixture must disclose both its own license and the provenance of the public failure shape it preserves.

subtasks.description: Retrieve TR-04 and apply its public-entry-point ownership-tracing rule
lessons: The 0.101 TR-04 match was specific enough to select the correct three-layer repair path before editing.

subtasks.description: Demonstrate the false-green gap and repair the correct delegation boundary
lessons: A legacy protocol-send test can remain green while an untested public control still dereferences stale ownership.

subtasks.description: Verify focused regression, legacy behavior, and Python compilation
lessons: Assert the terminal stream call and retain a related legacy test so both the new contract and existing protocol behavior are visible.

constraints: Use the public MIT-0 transfer fixture and its disclosed Apache-2.0 Tornado provenance only.
Do not edit or weaken the regression test.
Keep the production repair to channel.py and preserve the protocol ownership boundary.
Do not present controlled transfer evidence as a fresh upstream contribution.
lessons: Start at the named public control and trace each ownership hop; do not patch a plausible sibling surface merely because existing tests stay green.
The retrieved TR-04 experience transferred directly across domains from TCP_NODELAY to keepalive because the abstraction topology matched.
A focused terminal-call assertion exposes delegation gaps that broad legacy tests can miss.
Controlled fixtures support mechanism-level transfer claims, not broad real-world effectiveness or maintainer acceptance.

metrics.interpretation: One controlled transfer attempt succeeded. Retrieval matched the exact abstraction topology and informed the repair path; no unassisted control arm was run, so causal efficiency improvement is not measured.

limitations: The selected target is a dependency-free AEG transfer fixture, not a fresh checkout of an external project.
The fixture was explicitly designed from TR-04's abstraction shape, so a high retrieval match is expected and does not establish broad generalization.
No baseline arm was run; the claimed retrieval effect is a documented decision-path change, not a controlled causal performance estimate.
The added legacy test exists only in the isolated /tmp execution harness and is not proposed as a repository change.
No upstream acceptance or external contribution is involved.

designing a regression that distinguishes legacy green coverage from the missing public contract
evaluating topology-level transfer from a verified delegation repair
